News.title: Air coolers vs air conditioners: Cooling devices compared for summer
News.content:
After a sweltering May and a scorching hot June, this summer has been absolutely unbearable. Filled with heatwaves, we’re all desperately searching for the best way to keep cool.

From electric fans and air coolers to portable air conditioners, there are now more options than ever to beat the heat. While fans are still the most popular cooling device, many are turning to evaporative air coolers and portable air conditioners as a more powerful alternative, but which is worth your money?

If you're trying to decide between the two, here's everything you need to know before you buy, from how each one works to running costs, portability and cooling performance.



Air coolers vs portable air conditioners: How do they work and which cools a room more effectively?

Although they look very similar, air coolers and portable air conditioners work very differently. A portable air conditioner will actually lower the temperature of your home. An air cooler will make the air feel cooler, instead of removing the heat from your room.

Air coolers work by sucking warm air through a damp cooling pad before blowing it back into the room. The cooling pad uses water from an internal tank to stay wet. The colder the water in the tank, the cooler the air passing through the pad. Most models come with reusable ice packs that you can freeze and add to the water to boost the cooling effect, but you can always add your own ice cubes as well. These help keep the water, and therefore the cooling pad, colder, producing a cooler airflow than a standard fan.

Because air coolers rely on the power of evaporation, they work better in hot, dry and arid climates where moisture can evaporate easily. Think desert-like climates, where humidity can get as low as 40 per cent. Because they cool by evaporating water, the drier the air, the more moisture it can absorb.

Unfortunately, we’re not blessed with low humidity in the UK. With our increasingly humid summers, they become less and less effective. It’s not as easy for water to evaporate when humidity goes up. An air cooler produces less cooling in humid environments, but also adds even more moisture to your room.

On the other hand, portable air conditioners use a refrigeration system to physically remove heat from a room. Like an air cooler, portable air conditioners suck in the warm air. They then pass that air over cold evaporator coils to lower the temperature, before blowing the cooled air back into the room. The hot air that’s sucked up is then vented outside through an exhaust hose that you thread out of a window. Unlike an air cooler, a portable air conditioner physically lowers the temperature of the room.

You should also pay attention to the British Thermal Unit (BTU) ratings on each portable AC. The higher the BTU, the more powerful the air conditioner. You’ll want a higher BTU unit if you have a large space to cool, whereas lower BTU units wil be fine for bedrooms.

With all that said, portable air conditioners are the clear winner when it comes to cooling performance. While an air cooler can feel nice and chill when you’re sitting close, particularly when the climate is dry, a portable air conditioner cools your entire room down, no matter if the humidity is high or low.

DREO smart 3-in-1 portable air conditioner Although we haven’t tested this product ourselves, Dreo is a trusted home tech brand that we know delivers quality. The brand’s smart humidifier is our best overall option. The smart 3-in-1 portable air conditioner is one of the few air cons still in stock, which might be down to its hefty price tag of almost £600. However, this air con claims a super high powered 12,000 BTU cooling power with a 16ft radius, smart controls and silent function. £600 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary



Air coolers vs air conditioners: Which is cheaper to buy and run?

Because air coolers use the power of water evaporation, they’re much cheaper to run and cheaper to buy than portable air conditioners.

The cheapest air cooler in The Independent’s round-up of the best air coolers is the Sealey air cooler that costs £67. At the moment it’s out of stock but Dreo’s turbocool misting fan is one of the few remaining models available to buy and it’s £199.99.

DREO turbocool misting fan Dreo’s misting fan claims to reduce perceived temperature by six degrees celcius within 60 seconds. When our expert tester Joanne Lewsley put it to the test she praised how it delivered “powerful, whole-room cooling with ease.” She also enjoyed its misting feature and said, “the brand’s ultra mist tech works brilliantly, producing a super-fine mist that cools the air without leaving any dampness behind.” £190 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary

A portable air conditioner is significantly more expensive. The average price for a portable AC, using all of the ones in The Independent’s round-up is £350. The cheapest portable air conditioner in our list is the Blyss A018I-09C, which costs £280. And that portable AC has 9,000BTU. You can get a portable AC with 14,000 BTUs, and those cost much more.

And in terms of running costs? Air coolers are much cheaper to run than portable air conditioners. That’s because they’re essentially using a fan, water tank and cooling pad, rather than a compressor and refrigerant system to actively remove heat from the room.

In our own testing, the air coolers we tested used between 27W and 84W on their highest settings. That costs less than 1p to just over 2p per hour to run.

Portable air conditioners use considerably more energy, with energy experts previously telling The Independent that a typical unit costs around 20p to 60p an hour to run, depending on the model, energy efficiency and how often it’s used.

Most portable air conditioners in our own testing cost around £6 a week to run continuously when there’s a heatwave, although real-world costs are often lower because units cycle down once they reach their target temperature.

One other thing to keep in mind is that you’ll need to keep topping up the water tank in an air cooler to keep the breeze going, so think about water costs and the price of ice.



Air coolers vs air conditioners: Which is easier to use and more portable?

If you want sheer simplicity, air coolers are much easier to use and set up than a portable air conditioner.

Fill up the water tank, add some frozen ice packs for maximum cooling, then switch the air cooler on and choose a fan speed. Bob’s your uncle. Lots of the models we’ve reviewed also oscillate, boast timers and have a sleep mode. Some even connect to your phone for app controls.

Air coolers are also much more portable than portable air conditioners. Most of the models on our list weigh roughly 5kg, so they’re easy to carry around and move from room to room, similar to a regular pedestal or tower fan.

Portable air conditioners require a lot more set-up. Before you can use one, you need to attach an exhaust hose to the back (this can be fiddly). You then need to have it close enough to a plug point and a window, so that you can feed it through. You also need to seal the window so that no air comes through the sides, or it will be less efficient.

If you don’t use the exhaust hose, the hot air extracted from the room has nowhere to go – it’ll just end up heating your room even more.

And despite being called portable air conditioners, they’re not super portable. Most weigh around 15kg-20kg, so they’re difficult to lug around the house. While most are on casters, you’re still going to have a difficult time carting it from place to place. If you’re getting a portable air conditioner, you’re probably going to want to keep it in the same room.

If you want something you can easily move from your home office to the bedroom, an air cooler is much more portable. But if you're happy to spend a few minutes setting up a window kit for more powerful cooling, a bulkier portable AC might be the best choice for you.

Air coolers vs portable air conditioners: Which one needs more cleaning and maintenance?

Both air coolers and portable air conditioners need a little bit of handholding, though air coolers might need a little bit more.

With an air cooler, your main job is looking after the water tank and cooling pad. If you're using it regularly during a heatwave, you’ll want to empty any leftover water every few days and refill it with fresh water to help prevent bacteria, mould and unpleasant odours from developing. You'll also want to wipe down the water tank and clean the cooling pad according to the manufacturer's instructions, particularly before putting the unit away at the end of summer.

Portable air conditioners require some regular maintenance. though not quite as much as an air cooler. Most manufacturers recommend cleaning the filters every couple of weeks when you’re using it heavily. Dust build-up can restrict airflow and reduce cooling efficiency, so keeping the filters clean is important for maintaining performance. You’ll also need to give it a good clean after taking it back out following a long winter.

Should you buy an air cooler or a portable air conditioner?

It mainly comes down to your budget, whether you’ve got the right home set up and what you want from your cooling appliance.

Air coolers are much cheaper to buy and run than portable air conditioners, and they're lighter, easier to move around and require virtually no set-up beyond filling the water tank and adding the ice packs. That said, they’re definitely not as powerful as a portable air conditioner, essentially cooling the air it feeds out using water evaporation. It can also increase the moisture in your home.

Portable air conditioners, however, are in a whole different league when it comes to cooling performance. They actively remove heat from your room, meaning the temperature will actually be lowered, even during hot and humid weather. The trade-off is the price. They’re more expensive to buy and use much more electricity to run. They also require an exhaust hose to be vented through a window. But if you’re really struggling in the heat, a good portable AC could last a decade and still serve you well.

George Russell hit out at Mercedes in a furious radio rant following his retirement from the Belgian Grand Prix which has dealt a major dent to his world championship dream.

Russell trails team-mate Kimi Antonelli by 50 points after the Italian teenager romped to his sixth victory from the 10 rounds so far.

Russell’s race ended following a collision with Lewis Hamilton which arrived after he was exposed to the chasing pack following a first-lap engine glitch.

open image in gallery British driver George Russell trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

And in a radio transmission, which was not broadcast during Sunday’s race, Russell yelled: “What the f*** happened with the SOC (state of battery charge) down the straight?

“I had no f****** battery down the straight. Guys, unacceptable. Un-f******-acceptable, this whole weekend.”

Russell’s outing at Spa-Francorchamps was derailed by a deployment riddle within his Mercedes which contributed to him qualifying half a second behind Antonelli.

Russell had initially been told the problem was a result of his driving style, only for that theory to be ruled out by his baffled engineers.

Russell said he is “praying” Mercedes can find a solution in time for this weekend’s race in Hungary – the final round prior to the summer break – and added that he is now “numb to disappointment” following a catalogue of mechanical issues this year.

open image in gallery Antonelli won on Sunday to take victory tally for the season to six (Omar Havana/AP) ( AP )

Responding to Russell’s comments, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said: “You have to understand that a driver is very emotional when these situations happen, but on the other side, as a Formula One driver, you are part of a very elite group, and it is quite an honour to drive for Mercedes.

“I hope the numb feeling goes away and we will try to recreate that optimism and positivity.

“All of the drivers, or at least the ones I have worked have, have difficult spells and it happens to any sportsperson. You need to find a way of motivating or building up, and George has his way, and I am definitely trying to help him with that.

“I have known George for such a long time. I understand his frustration, and the team is 100 per cent behind him.”

Reflecting on Russell’s engine problem, Wolff continued: “The power units are so complex, the way you harvest, the way you deploy, and the interaction from the driver.

open image in gallery Toto Wolff said Mercedes are “100 per cent” behind Russell (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

“We have a super-strong package, and we are doing our best to fix the reliability problems, but with new regulations sometimes that happens.

“With George, there was definitely something on the engine that we have identified, that meant he had less energy to deploy into turn 18.

“It’s good that we spotted it here because, in Budapest, which is not an energy-starved circuit, it would have been more difficult to identify. But it still doesn’t make it better for him and that probably accounted for half the gap, or a little bit more, that he had to Kimi.”

News.title: Fans vs air conditioners: Which appliance to choose to beat the heat
News.content:
It’s already been a hot, hot summer. And with temperatures set to remain near 30C this week, it doesn’t look like it’s going to cool down any time soon. Thankfully, there are plenty of appliances out there that can help cool down your home during these prolonged heatwaves.

While drawing the curtains shut and opening the windows at night can help, an electric fan and a portable air conditioner are more effective at bringing the temperature down – if you can find one, that is. Earlier this month, Currys’ chief executive Alex Baldock warned that both appliances had been flying off shelves nationwide, making it tricky to find either cooling gadget.

But if you somehow manage to stumble on a fan or a portable air conditioner and it's in stock, which one should you get? While portable air conditioners are more effective at cooling a room, they also cost considerably more to buy and run. Fans are a lot cheaper and significantly quieter, but won't provide the same relief during a heatwave. Here's everything you need to know about the two, and how to decide which one is right for your home.



Fans vs air conditioners: How do they each work and which is more effective at cooling the room?

While both fans and air conditioners work to cool you and your home down, they each do so in a different way, and one is more effective than the other.

Electric fans don’t actually cool the air inside your home like portable air conditioners do, they cool you down instead. They do this by moving air around the room, helping sweat and moisture on your skin evaporate more quickly. The air being circulated by a fan is the same temperature as the air in the room, so while it creates a cooling sensation, it doesn’t lower the room temperature itself.

A powerful air circulator fan, such as the MeacoFan sefte (£99.99, Meaco.com), can help move air around an entire room and provide a strong cooling breeze, but it won't actually lower the room's temperature.

Portable air conditioners physically lower the temperature inside your home. They do this by sucking up the hot air in the room, cooling that air down and then expelling the excess heat through an exhaust hose. Air conditioners with higher British Thermal Unit (BTU) ratings are better suited to larger spaces, while lower-BTU models are best for smaller rooms.

On extremely hot days, a portable air conditioner, such as the Meaco meacocool MC series pro 8000 BTU (£380, Argos.co.uk), will be more effective at cooling an entire room because it actively extracts heat from the room and vents it outside. If you want the most powerful cooling, a portable air conditioner is significantly better than a fan.



Levoit tower fan While our favourite Levoit pedestal fan is currently out of stock, the tried-and-tested brand’s portable tower fan is currently available to buy at Amazon. The Levoit tower fan boasts a bladeless design, similar to a Dyson, it features four speed modes, 90-degree oscillation, a sleep mode and a 12-hour timer. It’s also fairly affordable at £60. £60 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary

Fans vs air conditioners: Which one takes up more room and which is more portable?

Electric fans win this one, hands-down. Handheld fans, desk fans, tower fans and even pedestal fans take up far less room than even the smallest portable air conditioners with the lowest BTUs.

While portable air conditioners are technically portable, featuring casters to help move them from room to room, they're still bulky and heavy. Even relatively compact models weigh more than 20kg, while larger units such as the ElectriQ ecoplus 10000BTU weigh almost 29kg. By comparison, many of the best fans we tested weighed between just 1kg and 5kg.

You also need to think about the exhaust hose, which needs to be threaded out of a window, and that can be a cumbersome, unwieldy process, especially if you’re using a window seal around the hose for maximum energy efficiency.

Fans, on the other hand, are lighter and much easier to move between rooms and they can be stored away more easily when summer comes to an end.

Dreo smart 3-in-1 portable air conditioner Although we haven’t tested this product ourselves, Dreo is a tried-and-trusted brand that we’ve tested multiple times at The Independent. And it’s one of the only portable ACs still in stock. Probably because of its hefty price tag of almost £600. However, this air con claims a super high powered 12,000 BTU cooling power with a 16ft radius, smart controls and silent function, so it’s very powerful. £600 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary



Fans vs air conditioners: Which costs more to run and how much energy does each use?

No surprises here, but fans are a lot cheaper to run than portable air conditioners. Based on our latest testing, most fans use between 13W and 40W of power at full speed. For example, the VonHaus air circulator uses around 13.6W and the MeacoFan sefte uses 22.5W. That’s only really a few pence to run overnight.

Portable air conditioners use considerably more energy because they actively remove heat from a room rather than simply circulating air. According to energy experts who spoke to The Independent, a typical portable air conditioner costs around 20p to 60p an hour to run, depending on the model, energy efficiency and how often it's used.

Our own testing revealed that most portable air conditioners would cost around £6 a week to run continuously when there’s a heatwave, although real-world costs are often lower because units cycle down once they reach their target temperature.

It's also worth remembering that efficiency isn't just about energy use. A portable air conditioner that cools a room quickly may ultimately cost less to run than a less effective model that needs to stay on for hours to achieve the same result.

You also have to think about the cost of the appliance itself. The cheapest fan in our latest round-up costs just £38. The best portable air conditioners we’ve tested start at £240 and can cost as much as £700. That cost increases for higher-capacity models with extra features.

I’d recommend investing in a smart AC controller, such as the Tado smart AC control V3+ (£100, Amazon.co.uk) if you’re going to install a portable air conditioner in your home as this will help you manage and control your unit so that it runs more efficiently.

Fans are cheaper to buy and cheaper to run, but that might mean very little when you’re struggling to work and sleep in the heat.

I’d also recommend keeping an eye on the energy rating when buying a portable air conditioner. “A” is the most energy efficient and “G” is the least energy efficient, so air conditioners with an A rating will be cheaper to run.



Fans vs air conditioners: Which one is easier to use?

Pedestal and desk fans are generally easier to use than portable air conditioners, but that's largely because they do fewer things. With a fan, you simply plug it in and select a speed setting.

That said, many fans now include sleep modes, eco settings, app controls, voice assistant support and temperature-responsive automation.

Portable air conditioners still require more setup, however. Firstly, you need to attach a hose to the back of the air conditioner and thread it out of the window so that the hot air can be expelled out of your room. This means that your window needs to be close to a plug outlet, otherwise you’ll have a few problems stretching the hose out of the window. You also need to use a window seal to help stop air from flowing back into your room when it’s on, or it’ll cool your place down more slowly and be less efficient overall.

They’re just packed with more features as well. Portable air conditioners can act as dehumidifiers, they include programmable timers and precise temperature controls, and some portable ACs, such as the Hisense APC09QC, even include smart cooling modes that automatically adjust its settings based on the room temperature.

I took into account the price, noise and cooling ability ( The Independent )

Fans vs air conditioners: Do you need to clean either one?

You should be cleaning an electric floor or desk fan once every three to four months, but considering most Brits will only be using a fan during the summer months, it’s worth giving a clean when you take it back out for the summer to remove any dust from the blades.

Portable air conditioners require more regular maintenance. Most manufacturers recommend cleaning the filters every couple of weeks when you’re using it heavily. Dust build-up can restrict airflow and reduce cooling efficiency, so keeping the filters clean is important for maintaining performance.

What are the different types of fan?

Unlike portable air conditioners, which are largely the same whatever model you choose, there are different types of fan out there, so what’s the difference between each one?

Tower fans are super-slim and have a small footprint, and plenty of them double up as air purifiers, or have support for app controls.

Pedestal fans usually deliver a stronger airflow, making them good for cooling larger spaces. Desk fans and portable fans are designed for personal cooling, making them ideal for home offices, bedside tables and travel.

Air circulator fans create a more consistent airflow ( Joanne Lewsley/The Independent )

Air circulator fans are also becoming popular options. They don’t just blow air in one direction, they move air around an entire room, creating more consistent airflow.

The last type of fan is a bladeless fan. Popularised by Dyson, they use hidden motors to create a stream of air without exposed blades. They’re quieter than bladed fans and are easier to clean, but they’re definitely more expensive.

Should you buy a fan or a portable air conditioner?

Each has its pros and cons. Portable air conditioners actively remove heat from a room and are the most effective option during periods of very hot weather. but they're bulkier, more expensive to buy and considerably more expensive to run.

Fans, on the other hand, circulate air to help sweat evaporate more quickly, making you feel cooler without actually lowering the room temperature. They're cheaper to buy, cheaper to run, easier to move around and simpler to store away after the summer.

Ultimately, the right choice comes down to your budget, the size of your space and how hot your home gets during summer. If you regularly struggle with high indoor temperatures, a portable air conditioner will deliver the best cooling performance. If you simply want a cost-effective way to stay comfortable, a fan may be all you need.

News.title: Chanel spent years creating a new Coco mademoiselle perfume – here’s my honest review
News.content:
In the (beautifully scented) world of perfumes, you’d be hard pushed to find a more prominent powerhouse than Chanel. So when I caught wind of the fact the coveted label is about to release a new fragrance, it piqued my interest.

Of course, the brand already boasts a number of best-selling women’s perfumes, with the likes of the original Chanel no.5 having reached heady heights in the olfactory hall of fame.

For me, Coco mademoiselle (£80, Boots.com) has always held a special place in my heart. My mum has worn the scent for as long as I can remember, so its bright notes of orange, jasmine and rose are instantly recognisable. Now, Chanel is launching a new iteration of this popular scent: Coco mademoiselle crush absolu.

Hitting shelves on 19 August (Gabrielle Chanel’s birthday), the new scent promises a sweeter trail, with notes of lychee and grapefruit. The question is: can it compete with the likes of the original Coco mademoiselle eau de parfum? More than a month before it’s set to go on sale, I put the new fragrance to the test.

News.content:

World Cup commentators are some of the best in their field when it comes to football, but that’s not always the case when it’s time to identify celebs in the stands – as the BBC’s Guy Mowbray showed.

The sports presenter, 54, mistook American pop star Pharrell Williams for A$AP Rocky during last night’s World Cup final, with many viewers at home picking up on his unfortunate blunder.

Spain took on Argentina during yesterday’s (Sunday 19 July) tense final, which saw the former claim the World Cup for the second time after winning 1-0 in extra time. It proved to be a star-studded event, with the likes of Jay-Z, Beyonce, Drake and Dua Lipa spotted in the crowd as well as comedian Will Ferrell, Dune star Timothée Chalamet and his girlfriend Kylie Jenner.

While “Happy” singer Pharrell Williams was enjoying the match at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, Mowbray incorrectly told BBC viewers that he was American rapper A$AP Rocky – or rather “AKA Rocky” – when the camera cut to him in the stands.

“I think that is AKA Rocky...or A$AP Rocky, sorry,” Mowbray said, speaking from the commentary box alongside ex-England player Alan Shearer.

Viewers were quick to pick up on the mistake, with one writing: “BBC Commentator just called Pharrell Williams ‘Asap Rocky’ wtf????”.

Another wrote: “BBC just called Pharrell Williams ‘AKA (ASAP) Rocky’,” alongside a face-palm emoji.

Musician and songwriter Williams, 53, is best known for appearing on hits like Daft Punk’s “Get Lucky”, his 2013 single “Happy”, and the Calvin Harris song “Feels”.

Meanwhile, A$AP Rocky – real name Rakin Mayers – is also an American musician, but shot to fame with his 2012 rap singer “F***in’ Problems”, later picking up three Grammy Award nominations.

open image in gallery Williams was mistaken for rapper A$AP Rocky ( Getty )

Mowbray isn’t the only commentator to misidentify a celebrity fan; Fox Sports announcer John Strong mixed up two of Hollywood’s biggest stars last night when he mistakenly identified The Odyssey’s Matt Damon as Fight Club’s Brad Pitt.

“Brad Pitt among the fans here,” Strong said confidently, before his fellow co-announcer, Stu Holden, corrected him: “That’s Matt Damon!”

They later joked about the blunder, with Strong saying: “I’m letting you take the rest of these guys. I got cocky after the first three, and I missed an absolute sitter, so I’m done.”

Damon took a break from his promotional duties for Christopher Nolan’s fantasy epic The Odyssey to attend the game with his Argentinian wife Luciana Barroso. The Odyssey comes 22 years after Pitt starred in the blockbuster Troy – based on another one of ancient Greek poet Homer’s works, the Iliad.

Last night’s Argentina-Spain game saw artists including Madonna, Shakira and Justin Bieber perform in an 11-minute half-time show – which was later slammed as “crap” by BBC presenter Wayne Rooney.

When asked by host Gabby Logan what his highlight from the show was, Rooney replied: “I’ll be honest, mine was when it finished. I like a lot of them artists but I thought it was crap.

“It just didn’t get me going and I wanted the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira, but that was too flat.”

News.content:

Broadcaster and journalist Edward Stourton has died aged 68, the BBC says.

Mr Stourton’s career spanned more than 40 years, including 10 years fronting the Radio 4 Today programme.

He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2014, but continued to work until recently.

The BBC said that he died on Saturday, surrounded by his family.

Jonathan Munro, the interim chief executive of BBC News and Current Affairs, said it was “far too soon to lose Ed”.

Mr Munro worked as his producer when he was ITN’s diplomatic editor.

open image in gallery The veteran newsreader, top left, died on Saturday surrounded by his family, the BBC said ( PA Archive )

The journalist was “unflappable then and ever after”, Mr Munro said.

“Many years later, I was listening to his superb analysis of the new Pope for the BBC – another of his many areas of expertise.

“Not many broadcasters can present Today, BBC One’s One O’Clock News, The World At One and Sunday – but he did. He leaves a huge gap.”

Mohit Bakaya, controller of BBC Radio 4, said: “Ed was an absolutely outstanding broadcaster.

“He brought intelligence, authority and an extraordinary hinterland to everything he did.

“When Ed was behind the mic, whether on Sunday or the various news programmes he regularly presented for Radio 4, you felt you understood the world that little bit better. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this sad time.”

open image in gallery Edward Stourton was a journalist and broadcaster for more than 40 years ( BBC )

Mr Stourton was born in Nigeria and was one of the founding members of the Channel 4 news team when it was formed in 1982.

Starting out as a scriptwriter, he went on to cover foreign news at the broadcaster as well as a stint as Washington correspondent, where he reported on the final years of Ronald Reagan’s presidency.

He then went on to join the BBC in 1988 before returning to ITN two years later as diplomatic editor, reporting from around the world including Baghdad during the Gulf War, Bosnia during the siege of Sarajevo and from Moscow in the final days of the Soviet Union.

He returned to the BBC in 1993 and fronted the One O’Clock News for six years and presented his own Radio 4 phone-in programme, Call Ed Stourton, before joining the Today programme in 1999.

Mr Stourton fronted the flagship current affairs programme for a decade. He later became a regular contributor.

Mr Stourton also worked as BBC Two’s world affairs strand correspondent, presented editions of Panorama as well as a series of Radio 4 programmes including The World At One, The World This Weekend and Analysis.

Along with his four-decade-long career as a broadcaster, he penned a number of books including 2013’s Cruel Crossing and his 2023 memoir Confessions – in which he revealed he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer nearly a decade earlier.

His most recent book, Made In America (2025), explores US history and how it has led to the era of Donald Trump. It was written to coincide with the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

Mr Stourton is survived by his wife Fiona and his four children.

News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine thuggery
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably, but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world, having beaten the favourites France in the last four.

Spain won this tournament for the second time, 16 years after the first. Now there is just one nation chasing a “second star”, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own, rather than Manchester City signing Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal with Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to to their system. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri, but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Argentina fans clash with police as riots erupt on streets of Buenos Aires after World Cup defeat
Sports.content:
VICIOUS riots erupted on the streets of Buenos Aires last night following Argentina’s agonising loss to Spain in the World Cup final.

Thousands gathered in the streets of the Argentinian capital to watch the match, but after the final whistle the losers’ frustrations boiled over.



Riots broke out at around 11.45pm when bitter fans clashed with cops on the streets.

At least 15 people were arrested, and several civilians and police officers injured, according to Argentine newspaper Infobae.



The brawl was sparked when several fans climbed over the protective fence of the Obelisk – a 67.5-meter-tall national monument.

Suddenly chaos broke out as fans began launching glass bottles and other objects at police.

Cops sprayed tear gas and used water cannons and rubber bullets in a desperate attempt to calm the mob.

Seven police officers sustained multiple injuries from the horror clash which lasted 20 minutes, the outlet reports.



Several people were also injured in the clashes, including a man who was kicked in the face by a rioter.

A woman also required medical attention but her condition remains unknown.

As police advanced from Corrientes Avenue to Belgrano Avenue and continued south through the city, the crowd began to retreat.



Images from the city show riot police armed with shields and batons storming through the streets littered with debris.

In one photograph a police man appears to be kicking a man on the ground.

Spain beat defending champions Argentina in their second-ever World Cup win last night.

But it was not just fans causing havoc after Ferran Torres secured a goal in extra time to hand Spain a 1-0 win.

Argentina’s own players caused a mass brawl on the pitch after their loss.



Seconds after the game ended Leandro Paredes went after Spain ace Gavi, throwing punches and lobbing him to the ground.

As a result of his behaviour, referee Slavko Vincic showed Paredes a red card.

And Manager Scaloni was also pictured in a confrontation with former Manchester City star Eric Garcia.



Despite the loss, Argentinians will be granted a national holiday.

President Javier Milei announced the move hours after Rodri lifted the World Cup trophy.

But the date will be decided by the national teams players and coaches, he added.

“Given the concern about the celebrations for the achievement reached by the Argentine National Team, I inform the population that, depending on what the players and the technical staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday.”

Sports.title: Tottenham star Cristian Romero totally blanks Donald Trump in awkward exchange after World Cup final
Sports.content:
CRISTIAN ROMERO snubbed a handshake with Donald Trump during the World Cup trophy ceremony.

Romero was on the losing side as Argentina were played off the park by Spain in a 1-0 win after Extra Time, courtesy of Ferran Torres‘ strike.



Like the rest of his team-mates, Romero went up onto the podium to collect his losers’ medal.

The medals were presented to the players by Fifa president Gianni Infantino and the three leaders of the host nations: Donald Trump, Claudia Sheinbaum and Mark Carney of the USA, Mexico and Canada, respectively.



However, after having his silver medal put over his shoulders by Infantino, Romero then SNUBBED a handshake with Trump.

The 28-year-old also looked like he was about to snub Mexican President Sheinbaum too after he shook the hand of Prime Minister Carney, the last of the three leaders in the line.



But the defender turned back to shake Sheinbaum’s hand as well.

President Trump did not seem to notice the snub as he was busy grabbing another medal to give to one of Romero’s team-mates.

Reacting on social media, fans were in uproar as one said: “Romero is a pure chaos merchant.”

A second said: “Hang on, he already had his medal from the other dude and shook his hand. Didn’t look like he intentionally tried to diss Trump?”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Another said: “Not sure Trump even noticed.”

A fourth said: “Romero aired Trump.”

Trump wasn’t quite done with his duties after handing out the winners’ medals to Spain as well.

The 80-year-old was also on hand to present the World Cup trophy to Spain afterwards.

There was an awkward exchange as he seemed to wait next to the squad as they prepared to lift the trophy, with Infantino rushing over to try and usher him away.



But Romero and Co would not have even noticed after they walked off the pitch as they refused to acknowledge Spain lifting the trophy.

The hot-headed Argies failed to muster a single shot at the Spanish goal in the 90 minutes of regulation time, while Enzo Fernandez was also given his marching orders for reckless and stupid foul on Pau Cubarsi.

Argentina had diligently defended up until then, but super-sub Torres soon broke the deadlock in the second half of Extra Time to give La Roja their second star.

It also means they will enter the 2030 tournament they are co-hosts of, alongside Morocco and Portugal with some matches also being played in South America, as defending champions.

Sports.title: Sore losers Argentina refuse to even acknowledge Spain lifting World Cup trophy and storm down tunnel straight after
Sports.content:
BITTER Argentina refused to watch Spain lift the World Cup trophy… then stormed straight off.

Lionel Messi and Co disgraced themselves in the final with their performance and behaviour.



They eventually registered their only two shots deep into the second half of extra time, by which time they were already 1-0 down and playing with ten men following Enzo Fernandez’s stupid red card for two yellows.

Tempers boiled over after the full-time whistle when Nahuel Molina, Leandro Paredes and Thiago Almada started fighting and punching the winners in a shocking mass brawl.



And there was clearly no love lost by the time Rodri got his hands on the trophy.

After waiting an age for the stage to be set up and Donald Trump to come out, Argentina received their runners-up medals from the US President and Fifa boss Gianni Infantino.

The squad then trudged over towards their own end of fans to take in their applause.

Heartbroken Messi stood aside on his own in floods of tears as they showed particular appreciation for their captain and hero, after what will most likely be his final World Cup match.

But then when Spain were invited forwards to collect their medals and lift the trophy, Argentina’s players did not even turn around.

They kept their backs to the stage in yet another classless gesture.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And within seconds of the confetti exploding over the champions, Argentina’s players gave one final clap to their supporters and walked off down the tunnel.

Earlier on, Lamine Yamal showed Argentina how it is done.

Amid the euphoria of Spain’s celebrations, he made a beeline to walk over to a dejected Messi sat on his own on the other side of the pitch.

The pair shared a warm embrace – 19 years on from their famous photoshoot when Yamal was a baby – and exchanged some words.

Ferran Torres’ finish was the only goal of a final which only one team tried to win.

Sports.title: World Cup final ratings: Lionel Messi does a disappearing act as Nico Williams steps off the bench to win it for Spain
Sports.content:
SPAIN sealed World Cup glory with an extra-time victory over Argentina – and it was two substitutes who made the difference.

Ferran Torres climbed off the bench to grab a 106th minute winner in the outskirts of New York.



The former Manchester City man reacted quickest following a knock-down from Nico Williams, who had a goal of his own controversially ruled out.

It allowed Spain to win the tournament for the second time – having also got their hands on the sport’s biggest prize in 2010.



And it ended Argentina’s hopes of defending the title they won in Qatar four years ago.

SunSport’s Shaun Custis and Dean Scoggins have given their verdict on the performances in the World Cup final

SPAIN

UNAI SIMON – 6/10

Not his busiest of days but undoubtedly has a composure about him and was always alert to the through ball. A calming influence for his defence.

PEDRO PORRO – 6

He has not always been an assured presence during Spurs’ struggles. However, he has certainly looked the part for Spain in this tournament both in defence and attack.

PAU CUBARSI – 7

What a talent this young defender is. Still only 19 yet he is an established centre-back for Barcelona and Spain. Wonderful passer of a football. Fouled by Enzo Fernandez who was sent off for a second yellow.

AYMERIC LAPORTE – 7

Seems to have found his form again since leaving Manchester City. Has established a good double-act with young Cubarsi and had a header saved by Emiliano Martinez.



MARC CUCURELLA – 7

There were those who thought he was a bit of a clown when he first signed for Chelsea. Has now joined Real Madrid and easy to see why. Gave Spain defensive quality as well as an attacking option.

RODRI – 7

What more can be said about Man City’s former Ballon d’Or winner? He controlled the midfield and frustrated his opponents, so much so Leandro Parades elbowed him in the back and was deservedly booked.

FABIAN RUIZ – 6

Has grown into one of the most versatile midfielders in football. Having won the Champions League at PSG, this was another big evening in his career but had a quiet game. Subbed off for Pedri.

DANI OLMO – 6

Took a hefty early challenge from Alexis Mac Allister, who seems to turn into rent-a-thug in a blue and white shirt. Olmo tried to be creative but was given a constant kicking.



ALEX BAENA – 5

It’s not easy to impress when your team-mates are usually looking for Lamine Yamal on the other flank and Baena struggled to get into the game here. Replaced by the far more effective Williams.

LAMINE YAMAL – 6

Was perhaps expected to make his mark on this World Cup more than he has. Showed flashes of his genius and had a free-kick well saved by Martinez.

MIKEL OYARZABAL – 5

Considering he is the go-to striker for one of the world’s best international teams he flies under the radar. Had one shot easily saved and took a nasty whack from Lisandro Martinez before being subbed.



SUBSTITUTES:

Ferran Torres for Oyarzabal (62mins) – 6

Spain needed a poacher to break the deadlock and Torres provided.

Pedri for Fabian Ruiz (62mins) – 5

Nico Williams for Baena (75mins) – 7

Was the star man. Attacking threat when he came on. Great nod back for the winner.



Mikel Merino for Olmo (75mins) – 5

Eric Garcia for Laporte (99mins) – 5

Martin Zubimendi for Rodri (99mins) – 5



ARGENTINA

EMILIANO MARTINEZ – 7

Excellent late save from Yamal in normal time before another stunner kept out Williams as he kept Argentina in it. Most of the other Spain shots were straight at him. Fumbled an Olmo shot on the hour and flapped at a corner. Organised his back line well.

GONZALO MONTIEL – 5

Bizarre mix of charging forward to occupy a right-wing position on the rare occasion Argentina had the ball, and charging back to try and get to Cucurella when they lost it. Good battle with Baena though. Subbed before the hour.

CRISTIAN ROMERO – 7

By far Argentina’s best player, on and off the ball. Coped with the Spain runners, made tackles and still found the energy to bark at anyone who came near him. Incredibly, the calm head in the backline this time until being subbed with injury.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ – 3

Very nervous start, almost poked into his own net from a Yamal shot and twice passed the ball out of play under no pressure. Injured himself with a poorly-timed tackle on Ruiz and got subbed. Saved from himself, really.

NICO TAGLIAFICO – 6

Good battle with Yamal, but struggled with his pace, fouling him on the halfway line the main tactic. Lucky to escape giving the ball away twice after the half-time snooze fest but stuck to his task well.



NICOLAS GONZALEZ – 3

Hooked at half-time after having little impact. One half decent dribble on the left but spent most of his time chasing Porro back to his own goal.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 5

Tireless effort and was run ragged by the Spanish. Little impact going forward, but none of the Argentines did. Was finally booked for backchat on 80 minutes and then was late on Cubarsi for a second yellow.

ALEXIS MAC ALLISTER – 6

Made a real impact… on Olmo’s legs, with two crunching first half tackles that somehow didn’t see a card. Worked incredibly hard to stay with the Spanish runners in midfield and tried, without much joy, to get them going in attack. Finally booked in extra-time.



RODRIGO DE PAUL – 5

Messi’s minder was more like Montiel’s minder in this one, spending half of his time doubling up going back to help his defence, with Cucurella providing plenty of problems. Industrious as ever.

JULIAN ALVAREZ – 4

More anonymous than Lionel Messi, if that was possible, with only eight touches in the first half. Crowded out most of the time in the second. Lots of runs, not many touches. Pressed so hard that most of the time Spain’s defenders just ran past him.

LIONEL MESSI – 4

The little magician did a disappearing act for most of the game as Argentina could not get him the ball. The usual classy touches but most of them to get his team out of their own half.

SUBSTITUTES:

Nicolas Otamendi for Martinez (44 mins) – 5

Absolute bruiser and took on Rodri at set-pieces. Held his line and kept Argentina battling. Stayed strong and clung onto runners, literally. Dived to get Spain’s goal disallowed in extra-time.



Leandro Paredes for Gonzalez (46 mins) – 3

Booked for his first involvement – a barge off the ball on Rodri. Similar to what he did most of the game against England. Another lunge on Porro later before fouling Torres. Was eventually sent off during a mass brawl after the final whistle.

Nahuel Molina for Montiel (58 mins) – 6

Secured the right-side when he came on and the Baena-Cucurella attacks subsided afterwards.

Facundo Medina for Romero (70 mins) – 6



Replaced Romero on 70 minutes, but played left centre-back. Did a good job against Torres with Argentina’s backs to the wall. Some big, fair tackles.

Giuliano Simeone for De Paul (70 mins) – 6

Nasty foul on Cucurella late on, having replaced De Paul. Did his defensive work against the Spain left-back.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Marcos Senesi for Alvarez (102 mins) – 4

On for Alvarez to try and play for penalties. Couldn’t block Torres’ shot.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan leads fan fury at Argentina star Leandro Paredes and blasts Argentina as ‘disgrace to football’
Sports.content:
PIERS MORGAN led the stinging criticism of the Argentine “thugs” who lost to Spain in the World Cup final.

Chaos erupted after Spain‘s extra-time victory, with Argentina‘s Leandro Paredes involved in a nasty scuffle.



Paredes completely lost his head as he sprinted over and shoved Eric Garcia to the ground.

As others from both sides charged over, the Argentine midfielder took aim at Gavi, dragging him to the ground and then striking him while he was down.



Referee Slavko Vincic showed Paredes a straight red card despite the game already being over.

And Arsenal and England fan Morgan had seen enough to let rip on social media.

He wrote on X: “Disgusting behaviour by the Argentinians at the end, especially Paredes.

“Just a bunch of nasty violent thugs, and a disgrace to football. Never been so happy to see a team lose.”

Argentina had made themselves more unpopular among England fans during the two nations’ semi-final on Wednesday.

Valentin Barco and Cristian Romero both celebrated goals in the faces of England players, and Argentina toasted the victory with a banner about the Falklands.



So plenty of other fans were happy to join the pile-on when Spain prevailed.

One punter wrote: “They should never be allowed to contest these tournaments again.”

Another added: “Disgusting team! A Spanish win is the right result for football.”

And a third chimed in with: “No place for that kind of behaviour in football.”

Sports.title: Awkward moment Infantino forced to rescue Trump as he lingers on stage while World Cup winners Spain wait to lift trophy
Sports.content:
DONALD Trump was caught out almost photobombing the victorious Spanish team as he lingered on the stage while they patiently waited to lift the World Cup.

The president couldn’t seem to resist hovering onstage after handing over the trophy as the Spanish side celebrated their win over Argentina, with Fifa boss Gianni Infantino forced to rush back to guide him away.



Trump joined Fifa President Infantino at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey to present the trophy to the Cup winners after their 1-0 win on Sunday.

The President handed out gold medals to Spain and the referees, as well as silver medals to Argentines.



He was joined onstage by the leaders of his co-host nations – Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum.

But after handing out the trophy with Infantino, Trump didn’t appear to want to get out of Spain’s shot.



Infantino walked off one side of the stage as the Spaniards waited to hoist the cup, but Trump continued to talk to the players before standing to the side of the team.

Some of the Spanish team even looked like they were going to coax Trump into his famous YMCA dance.

The Fifa boss jogged back across the stage as he tried to usher Trump to the side.

He eventually succeeded as the Spanish team began their celebrations to roars from thousands in the crowd.



Trump could be seen again pausing at the side of the stage as he watched gold ticker tape rain down on the winners.

Spain beat defending champions Argentina in their second-ever World Cup win.

Trump watched the game from a box with his fellow world leaders and Infantino while protected by bullet-proof glass.

Football superfan son Barron was also in attendance, and chatted to Infantino and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney before the game.

First lady Melania Trump beamed as the crowd greeted her, wearing a bomber jacket with a red, white, and blue collar.



It came after Trump issued a request to Infantino to allow the World Cup to return to the US “immediately.”

“Based on the numbers we will be requesting it immediately,” he told Fox Sports.

“We have to do this again, and we have to do this again while I am around, hear that Gianni?”

Under Fifa rules, the US would not be eligible to host until 2038.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney claims Argentina 'deserved' World Cup final heartbreak
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney claims Argentina 'deserved' World Cup final heartbreak

Argentina didn't take defeat well in the World Cup final after being outclassed for two hours by Spain as Wayne Rooney insists they got everything they deserved

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney didn't hold back in his assessment of Argentina (Image: BBC)

Wayne Rooney suggested that Argentina "got what they deserved" after losing to Spain as he lamented their "sad" reaction to coming up short in the World Cup final.

‌



Throughout their run to the showpiece event the Argentines have copped criticism for their hugely physical approach, with some citing their willingness to engage in the game's dark arts.

‌



Before producing quality in the final half an hour against England, Argentina's antics didn't impress everyone in their semi-final and they kept that up in the final, where they were firmly second best to the Spanish. Fernandez saw red in the second-half and Rooney has hammered their approach, with tensions boiling over once the full-time whistle had gone and their era as world champions was ended.

‌



He said: “We’ve seen it with Argentina before. It’s not the reaction you want. We saw it after knocking England out in the last round as well. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves. It’s disappointing. That’s just sad.

Argentina players show true colours with response to Spain lifting the World Cup READ MORE :

Tottenham star Cristian Romero 'snubs' Trump handshake after World Cup final READ MORE :

”If you lose a game, get out of there. That’s just not good enough. It’s a reaction to them being outplayed, outfought, outthought. They resort to that at the end. It’s sad.”

Leandro Paredes was also shown a red card for throwing punches at Spanish stars Eric Garcia and Gavi after the full-time whistle. Spanish players raced onto the pitch to celebrate when Argentinian defender Nahuel Molina appeared to punch Rodri in the stomach.

‌



Joe Hart, also on BBC duty with Rooney, was on the same page as the ex-England striker and hammered the Argentine's for their behaviour.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez received his marching orders (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“It’s disgusting,” he said. “There was one man on the pitch who did have class and it was Lionel Messi. He shook hands with every one of the Spanish players. The game is done. They can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.

Article continues below

“Rodri didn’t need to get in their faces, but when you’ve been wound up for 120 minutes, and you’ve felt wronged with the referee on your back, you’ve got that win, the referee has blown his whistle, leave it.”

Sports.title: Alan Shearer calls for major rule change during Spain vs Argentina World Cup final
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer calls for major rule change during Spain vs Argentina World Cup final

BBC Sport pundit Alan Shearer shared his idea to fix a problem he spotted during the World Cup final

View 2 Images Alan Shearer called for a rule change during the World Cup final (Image: Michael Driver | MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Alan Shearer proposed a rule change during the World Cup final to help combat grappling at corner kicks. Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to clinch the famous trophy for the second time in their history.

‌



The new world champions dominated the game but had to wait until the 106th minute for Ferran Torres to break the deadlock in extra time. Argentina did not have a shot at goal until the 117th minute as Lionel Scaloni’s side looked to edge their way to victory.

‌



The 2022 World Cup winners committed 24 fouls to Spain’s 21 across the match but former England captain Shearer took issue with one offence that was not officially deemed a foul. The incident came in the build-up to a Spanish corner, taken by Nico Williams in the 78th minute.

‌



As Williams delivered his cross, referee Slavko Vincic blew his whistle to warn Argentina defender Facundo Medina about fouling Spain players before the ball was in play. This did not sit well with Shearer, who was on TV commentary for BBC Sport, and the Newcastle United legend shared his idea to fix the issue.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“This is what I mean about referees, they’re the biggest time-wasters of the lot,” Shearer said. “If that ball was in play once it’s put on to the grass [quadrant] then that would stop that entirely.”

‌



Gabby Logan warns Micah Richards on BBC's World Cup final coverage after Gary Lineker jibes READ MORE :

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has new motive for 64-team World Cup as truth laid bare READ MORE :

The subsequent corner from Williams sailed over his teammate Pau Cubarsi’s head but Shearer did highlight a loophole for defensive teams at corners. The International Football Association Board (IFAB) allowed FIFA to use VAR reviews for attacking fouls at set pieces if they directly led to a goal, penalty or disciplinary action.

Following a review, the set piece would then be retaken as free-kicks cannot be awarded for incidents which occur when the ball is not technically in play. Therefore, the same rules were applied to defensive offences, as a penalty cannot be awarded to the attacking team.

In May, ahead of the World Cup an IFAB statement read: "The IFAB has approved a clarification to the video assistant referee protocol for use at the 2026 FIFA World Cup regarding clear offences committed by the attacking team before the ball is in play at a corner kick or free kick that have a direct impact on a goal, penalty kick, or disciplinary sanction.

‌



View 2 Images Slavko Vincic refereed the World Cup final (Image: Alex Livesey - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"If the offence meets the criteria set out in the clarification, VAR will recommend an on-field review, following which, if the referee determines that an offence occurred before the ball was in play, the appropriate disciplinary action will be taken and the corner kick or free kick will be retaken."

An example cited by Pierluigi Collina, now FIFA's chief refereeing officer and chairman of the FIFA referees committee, was Ben White's goal for England against Uruguay in March. Adam Wharton blocked a defender’s path before the corner had been taken but the referee was unable to disallow the goal.

Article continues below

The rule change for attacking fouls at set pieces is due to be reviewed by IFAB following the conclusion of the World Cup. VAR teams were also given the remit to ensure corners were correctly awarded, aided by new technology, but this was not applied to wrongly awarded goal kicks that should have been corners.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal makes a fool of Donald Trump during awkward moment at trophy presentation
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal makes a fool of Donald Trump during awkward moment at trophy presentation

Lamine Yamal and Donald Trump had a frosty exchange

View Image Lamine Yamal appeared to leave President Donald Trump hanging when he initially refused to shake his hand (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

World Cup-winner Lamine Yamal almost made a mockery of Donald Trump in front of millions following Spain's win over Argentina. The 19-year-old played a crucial role in Sunday's final in New Jersey before he appeared to snub the president of the United States.

‌



Yamal was on his way to the trophy presentation stage at New York/New Jersey Stadium after Spain's dramatic 1-0 in extra time. Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino awaited the youngster on-stage, along with a queue of Spanish dignitaries.

‌



But the Barcelona winger looked noticeably reticent to the prospect of shaking hands with the president. He first clasped hands with Infantino and gave the FIFA chief a friendly embrace with his free arm.

‌



By contrast, Trump's extended arm went unanswered for a moment as Yamal seemed to take stock of who it was greeting him. Yamal put his hand out, then retracted it ever so slightly as if he was going to snub Trump. Eventually, however, the Spanish talisman reciprocated the greeting along with a subtle nod in Trump's direction.

Yamal then dipped his head to receive his winner's medal before accepting his congratulations from some of Spain's representatives. King Felipe VI was among those warmly congratulating the winning side, as well as runners-up Argentina.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Lionel Messi bursts into tears after Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain READ MORE :

Yamal's reaction to the King of Spain couldn't have been more different to his meeting with Trump. His blank, emotionless expression almost immediately gave was to a broad grin as he was drawn in by his countryman prior to lifting the trophy.

Both Trump and Infantino were roundly booed by the New Jersey audience as they took to the field for the trophy presentation. That's largely been the case for any match Trump and his FIFA cohort have attended throughout the tournament.

His appearance was also jeered after being shown on the big screen following Sunday's national anthems. While the drama and quality of football at World Cup 2026 may have received positive reviews, the same can't be said for the cost and general organisation in other aspects.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Supporters have been hugely critical of the expense at this World Cup, including inflated public transport costs and general ticket prices. While those topics may not be of major concern to Yamal, La Roja's shining light looked anything but overjoyed to meet the US leader.

Argentina defender Cristian Romero took it one step further by completely blanking the US president. Romero accepted his runner-up medal on stage but refused to shake Trump's hand altogether in what looked a very intentional snub.

‌



Yamal didn't sparkle quite as some expected at this World Cup following his heroics en route to victory at Euro 2024. He entered the competition on the back of an injury and finished the tournament with just one direct goal contribution in eight games.

He did, however, play a hand in setting up Ferran Torres' extra-time decider on Sunday night. And the teen talent was nonetheless vital in Spain's possession tactics as he helped deliver the World Cup in a country where he still can't legally drink alcohol.

Yamal's cold reaction to Trump wasn't the last of the president's final faux pas, either. He was also criticised for lingering on stage as he sought to share the spotlight with Spain during the trophy lift before he quietly departed alongside Infantino.

Sports.title: Argentina facing double punishment after 'disgusting' scenes in World Cup final defeat
Sports.content:
Argentina facing double punishment after 'disgusting' scenes in World Cup final defeat

Argentina had two players sent off during their defeat to Spain in the World Cup final in New Jersey with Enzo Fernandez and Leandro Paredes getting red cards

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes was sent off after the final whistle of the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Argentina are facing the prospect of being hit with a double punishment following the red cards handed to Enzo Fernandez and Leandro Paredes in the World Cup final. Spain claimed a 1-0 victory over the defending champions to win the tournament at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Extra time was needed to determine the winner after the match finished goalless after 90 minutes, with former Manchester City star Ferran Torres scoring the winning goal. Fernandez was sent off during the closing moments of normal time after picking up two yellow cards before the end of the 90 minutes.

There were chaotic scenes after the final whistle as Paredes was also shown a red card after kicking Eric Garcia to the floor and appearing to place his hand around the Spain defender’s throat during a heated confrontation, before going on to push Gavi to the floor.

Argentina will now see both players serve a suspension but it remains to be seen how long the duo will be unavailable for selection. Fernandez’s situation is clearer, with two yellows typically resulting in a one-match suspension, which will be expected to be handed to the Chelsea midfielder.

Lionel Messi bursts into tears after Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain READ MORE :

World Cup final ends in chaos as Argentina star throws punches after Spain win READ MORE :

For Parades, there is the prospect of a lengthier ban due to the nature of his sending off after the final whistle. Due to the World Cup now being over, the suspensions handed to the Argentina duo will be expected to come into effect for the country’s next competitive fixture.

“Any suspension that cannot be served during the FIFA World Cup 26 will be carried over to the representative team’s next official match in accordance with the relevant provisions of the FIFA Disciplinary Code,” FIFA rules state.

Former Newcastle United striker Alan Shearer was on commentary duty for the BBC’s coverage of the final in New Jersey and gave his verdict on the post-match scenes.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them," Shearer said. "There is no place or space for that.

View 2 Images Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for kicking and punching Spanish stars (Image: (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images))

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Manchester United legend Gary Neville was also clear with his verdict while on punditry duty for ITV.

"It's a disgrace,” Neville said. “I love the competitiveness of the Argentines, fighting and scrapping for their lives, Messi has propped them up, but it’s been a disgrace the last few games.”

Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart also gave a blunt verdict. “There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players,” he said on the BBC.

“The game’s done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.”
