Tuchel, who signed a contract extension before the tournament, has been criticised heavily for his tactics against Argentina when he opted to switch to a back five to try to defend a 1-0 lead.

Kane admitted England had fallen short against Lionel Scaloni’s side but described the environment Tuchel has created since succeeding Gareth Southgate in 2025 as “the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness”.

The captain said: “I know there are a lot of questions after the other night. We have to process it as players. I’m sure the manager will. It’s his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel.

“There are also a lot of things as players we can learn from the other night. For now it’s just trying to process everything. We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.

“Fans are going to be angry and we understand it. It’s a major tournament and that’s why you dream so big. When it doesn’t go your way you have to take the criticism. We’re all willing to do that, to dare to reach the biggest goal of all. We know over the next two years until we’re facing that situation again there is always going to be a question mark. It’s something we have to take and use as motivation.”

England missed out on facing regular top-class opposition in the buildup to the World Cup after being relegated from the top Nations League group in 2022 under Southgate. They were promoted in 2024 and will face Spain, Croatia and Czechia, starting with a rematch of the Euro 2024 final against Luis de la Fuente’s side on 26 September at Wembley. After beating France – albeit in a largely meaningless game – Kane thinks England must take the competition seriously if they are to thrive in tournaments.

View image in fullscreen Defeat to an established opponent was a familiar feeling for England. Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images

“The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be,” he said. “We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments. The bottom line is we lost anyway. It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations. We can train, play the qualifiers … I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“Getting used to those big environments and finding our best form against those teams, like we did against France, albeit not in the most competitive match. We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Kane has been on the losing side in two World Cup semi-finals and two European Championship finals and he believes Tuchel is the man to help England to make the final step.

“The enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has … it doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time. We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach. He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year. That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way.

“Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself. We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks. It won’t be until the next camp where you think about what the future holds and what the next target is. We’ll have conversations as captain and manager and with other teammates and staff, to see where we can be better.”

Sports.title: Emotional Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni storms out of press conference in TEARS after admitting World Cup final defeat 'hurts his soul'
Sports.content:
Emotional Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni storms out of press conference in TEARS after admitting World Cup final defeat 'hurts his soul'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni hastily left his press conference in tears after their World Cup final defeat to Spain.

The 48-year-old was aiming to become only the second manager to retain the trophy after spearheading Argentina's 2022 triumph in Qatar.

But Ferran Torres' extra-time strike saw Spain crowned World Champions for a second time, with Luis de la Fuente’s side winning the European Championship and World Cup back-to-back.

Reflecting on the tournament, Scaloni said: ‘To be where I am today is a dream come true.

‘We tried right up to the very end to give it our all - both the coaching staff and the players. I think it’s only right to take this time to think about it all.

‘It’s a beautiful position to be in. Somewhere where I dreamed of being. So to carry on, lots of things are necessary.’

He fought back tears before eventually folding.

‘Above all, we need time to reset and form another group like this one. It’ll be hard to recreate this one. It hurts my soul, I’m sorry,’ Scaloni said as he left the press conference crying.

Following their World Cup final defeat to Spain, Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni walked out of his post-match press conference after becoming too emotional to carry on. pic.twitter.com/c7NQjN2MG8 — BBC Sport (@BBCSport) July 20, 2026

Scaloni has just five months left on his Argentina deal. Considering his future, he spoke as though the end is near, but committed to seeing his contract out.

‘I will talk to the president,’ he said. ‘I have an idea of what I would like to do.

‘I will see out my contract and I feel the need, I don't know if something as big can be done. We need to speak this through.

‘I am thankful to the president for bringing me this chance of being in this place where I am at the moment.

‘It was a dream place for everyone. We have tried up until the very last minute to give our utmost, the staff and players.

‘I believe it's only fair that I can take this time for myself to think this through.’

Sports.title: Bitter Argentina players turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift after violence marred winners' celebrations - as lip-reader reveals what furious star said to winning captain Rodri during brawl
Sports.content:
Bitter Argentina players turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift after violence marred winners' celebrations - as lip-reader reveals what furious star said to winning captain Rodri during brawl

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina's sulking stars refused to acknowledge World Cup victors Spain's trophy lift in New York on Sunday with players spotted turning their backs to the newly-crowned champions.

The 2022 winners were outplayed by Luis De La Fuente's side in a drab encounter at the MetLife Stadium, with Lionel Messi's side unable to disrupt their rivals with the same aggressive, physical tactics that unsettled England in the semi-final.

Barcelona star Ferran Torres bagged the winning goal in extra time to seal the European nation's second World Cup triumph after first winning the trophy in 2010, leaving Messi, 39, in tears at the final whistle.

The defeated finalists collected their silver medals from FIFA supremo Gianni Infantino and US President Donald Trump on the stage at the MetLife Stadium but opted not to watch as Spain lifted the trophy - which is customary in finals of major tournaments.

Instead, the Argentina players, coaching team and staff walked over to the end where the majority of their fans were located and decided not to watch their rivals celebrate their title.

Footage shows Spain players holding the World Cup trophy aloft as gold confetti explodes behind them, with the Argentina team facing the other way.

The scenes came after the final descended into violence following Torres's extra-time winner in New Jersey.

Argentina players decided to turn their backs to Spain's World Cup trophy lift on Sunday

The move came after ugly scenes at the end of the game which Spain won 1-0 after extra time

After the final whistle, fights broke out between the two teams. Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their victory.

Torres scored a 106th-minute winner after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off in the 93rd minute following a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsi - which summed up the South Americans' deplorable approach to the game.

At full time, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about Las Rojas' pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

Messi's side had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with Rodri raising concerns before the New York contest.

'You and [Spain team-mate Aymeric] Laporte. Both of you,' he said to Rodri.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨دازن إسبانيا تنشر ما قاله أوتاميندي لرودري بعد نهاية المباراة:



ابدأ بالحديث بشكل أقل يا رجل فقد قضيتما الأسبوع بأكمله تبكيان. طوال الأسبوع وأنتما تبكيان.



أنت ولابورت. كلاكما.

هذا أمر لا يُفعل.

قضيتما الوقت تبكيان وتشتكيان من الحكام يا صديقي.

لكن كان يجدر بك ألا تتحدث… pic.twitter.com/bWY9efhdOH — ZidaneModric10 (@said_modric10) July 20, 2026

Spain shared fears of roughhouse tactics from Argentina, and their concerns came to fruition with Enzo Fernandez sent off for a shocking challenge on Pau Cubarsi

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been when they beat England in the semis.

Astonishingly, Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow, despite it being a clear foul, before attempting to get Spain rival Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his face while talking to Messi.

New laws state that footballers who cover their mouths when speaking to a player from the opposing team must be sent off, but replays showed Cucurella was simply scratching his nose as he spoke to Argentina's captain.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off for a second bookable offence in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-gasp free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those came in the 117th minute.

Donald Trump took centre stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away - but the President remained where he was

Elsewhere, Trump took centre stage during the trophy lift, with the US President refusing to step aside to allow the victorious Spaniards to have their moment in the spotlight.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained where he was.

He stood to the side of the team as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5 to 1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage once again.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the pair undoubtedly clear.

Fans noted that one Argentina star - Tottenham defender Cristian Romero - completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from Infantino before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, the President also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball - which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

There was a degree of irony in regards to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

Wayne Rooney savaged the 2026 World Cup final halftime show as he described the performance as 'c**p' and said the 'best part was when it ended' live on BBC

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, with the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and the Muppets all performing under one roof

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite - alongside FIFA President Infantino, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump also shook hands with Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the president. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, reportedly watched the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the President's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

The World Cup final also saw a bizarre half-time show, with Madonna, Coldplay, Justin Bieber, The Muppets and Shakira performing during the 27-minute interval, which was described by Wayne Rooney as 'c**p'.

'To be honest, mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Sports.title: Trump's cringe World Cup cameo was a fitting finale to a tournament blighted by excess, greed and FIFA boss Gianni Infantino's twisted dreams
Sports.content:
Night was closing in over New Jersey. The smog had cleared, the storms had passed, the fireworks had stopped crackling and the spotlight had shifted a few meters away from a vast presentation crew headlined by Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino.

Only then – at nearly 7pm local time, at long, long last - could Spain captain Rodri thrust the World Cup trophy toward the setting sun. It had been nearly six weeks since Mexico and South Africa lit the fuse on this World Cup. It had been nearly four hours since this final kicked off and more than five hours since the festivities began.

In that time, Spain took 120 minutes to beat Argentina but Infantino needed even longer to crowbar in all the manifestations of his twisted dreams.

How smug the FIFA president looked as he ignored the boos and stood beside Trump to crown the new world champions. How cringeworthy it was to watch them hand over the trophy together. And how unfortunate that – as gold glitter fell from the sky – Trump and Infantino refused to exit stage left and let the real heroes of this story have their moment.

But who expected any different on a day when sports was – time and again – barged into the shade by politics and music and the circus of showbusiness?

Only FIFA and its Teflon president know why Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal and Co needed to share soccer's greatest stage with Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, Coldplay, the Muppets and a clown.

Spain celebrate their World Cup triumph while President Donald Trump stands nearby

The FIFA president and the US president handed over the World Cup trophy together

Madonna, flanked by Ronaldinho (L) and Ronaldo (R), performed during the halftime show

Shakira sung Dai Dai with Burna Boy during halftime of Spain's win over Argentina

But whatever the motivation – and some guesses are better than others – this will be remembered as a final but also a first. A first World Cup final to feature a halftime show. A first World Cup final where fans could pay $1million to watch from a pitchside sofa. A first World Cup final when, apparently, soccer wasn't enough.

It was, in many ways, a fitting apex to a tournament when the sport nearly drowned under a tidal wave of greed.

For much of this summer, the performances of superstars such as Messi and Jude Bellingham ensured this World Cup has been a triumph in spite of FIFA. There will be some who sat through these 120 minutes and concluded that Spain and Argentina needed an added dose of drama and sparkle.

But, unfortunately for Infantino, his halftime show, his closing ceremony and the rest of his add-ons fell flat, too. History suggests that won't be enough for him to change tack.

Not even the haze which has hung over New York in recent days could blur the grimmer aspects of this World Cup. When the child mascots were sponsored by Quaker Oats. When the prize was delivered on to the field in a Louis Vuitton 'Trophy Trunk.' When some fans were barred from entering the country and many others were priced out of going to games. When organizers are selling everything from commemorative rings to a patch of MetLife grass for $450.

On Sunday, adverts for the halftime show were plastered across the walls of the men's toilets. Perhaps the urinals will be the next souvenir to hit the market. That might be all an average fan could afford. This was, after all, among the priciest sporting events in history with some tickets – on FIFA's own resale platform – going for up to $2.3m in recent days.

Perhaps those with the deepest pockets want more for their money than 120 minutes of soccer. And at the end of the first half, the players had barely reached the tunnel when Bruce Buffer appeared on the jumbotrons and began a five-minute countdown to 'what we've all been waiting for.' That scripted line rather summed up FIFA's warped priorities this summer.

Ferran Torres scored the winning goal for Spain as they overcame Argentina in extra time

Justin Bieber sang a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah on Sunday

Trump and Infantino watched the game together from a luxury suite at MetLife Stadium

For those who missed it, here is a brief run-through of 27 forgettable minutes: Madonna opened the show, 'driven' around the bowels of the stadium by Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

The 67-year-old made it to the edge of the field but no further before K-Pop band BTS took over. Before long, Ted Lasso was introducing Justin Bieber. His a capella performance was followed by Shakira and Burna Boy's rendition of 'Dai Dai.'

The final act of the 11-minute show belonged to a local choir, PS22 Chorus, who performed with Coldplay while the Muppets had a cameo, too. Production wise, it wasn't a patch on the Super Bowl.

So what did the crowd make of it? Well, England legend Wayne Rooney – watching from the BBC studio in the stands – called it 'crap' and supporters of both Spain and Argentina made their feelings clear, too. As soon as the music stopped, they broke into song and attempted to turn this into a soccer game once more.

Perhaps it should come as no surprise that FIFA chose this summer to turn the World Cup final into a spectacle resembling the Super Bowl. Over here, the lines separating sports, music and celebrity culture are more blurred than perhaps anywhere else. But there was still a heavy dose of irony in their decision.

Because back in 1994, the last time the USA hosted the World Cup, organizers attempted to put on a halftime show. Whitney Houston was supposed to perform on the field. Alas, FIFA torpedoed that plan and their idea to sell final tickets for $1,000.

It turns out US soccer chiefs were on to something. That day at the Rose Bowl, organizers also devised – what they claim was - sports' first ever hospitality package. It wasn't much – fans received a parking pass, a program and some hors d'oeuvres. But three decades on, this circus, these $1m sofas, were a garish illustration of what can happen when you open Pandora's Suite.

Trump and Infantino opted for a box rather than a couch and it is fortunate this was the first and only game the US president attended. Because by midmorning, the perimeter of MetLife Stadium had descended into chaos. As the sun burned overhead, lines snaked around parking lots and tempers began to boil over.

Influencer IShowSpeed was among those to perform at the closing ceremony on Sunday

Tom Cruise delivered a speech before the game that was largely drowned out by supporters

Agents from the Department of Homeland Security, state police, and Transportation Security Administration were on hand to help the secret service check everyone and everything coming inside. Among the items that had to be 'surrendered' at the gates? Bicycles, balloons and, in a real blow to any influencers posing as soccer fans, selfie sticks.

It is a well-polished routine by now – since returning to the Oval Office, the president has barely missed a major sporting event on these shores. But the exhaustive security operation still led to long delays. All to keep one man safe. All for Trump to miss the closing ceremony. How will he ever forgive himself?

There was around an hour and a half until kickoff when some of Spain's squad decided to take in their surroundings. Moments after they wandered off the field, a small army went to work. They covered the pitch with a giant flag depicting many of New York's most iconic monuments; they erected a small golden stage in the center circle. They were orchestrated by a maniac in fluorescent green who gesticulated with all the aggression of a North Korean army general.

How to describe the next 15 minutes? There were plenty of pyrotechnics. There were also performances by the influencer IShowSpeed, who danced and mimed his way around the field, and Post Malone, who closed the show after walking through a corridor of fire.

Trump and Infantino greet new World Cup winner and rising superstar Lamine Yamal

Infantino and Trump also fawned over Lionel Messi as they handed him a runners-up medal

Off went the flag and on came the corner flags to be stuck back into the ground. That was a timely reminder that a soccer match would soon break out. Alas, the end of the closing ceremony did not mean an end to the noise. And so resumed the adverts, the music, the invitations for fans to turn up the volume. No doubt they would have obliged if they had been given some silence to fill.

Instead? As kickoff approached, we heard from Coldplay's Chris Martin, who addressed the crowd in broken Spanish, from Nicole Scherzinger and Robbie Williams, whose performance was interrupted by a four-jet flyover, and from Tom Cruise, whose speech was – mercifully – drowned out by the Argentina supporters.

By then, Trump had announced his arrival. A fleet of helicopters including Marine One fluttered over MetLife Stadium and before long, the president was sitting on halfway with only bulletproof grass obstructing his view of this final.

After extra time, he was joined on the field by Canadian prime minister Mark Carney, Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum and other dignitaries. Trump handed over winners' medals to Spain as, a few meters away, tears filled Messi's eyes. This was not the ending that the Argentina captain wanted. In truth, this is not what anyone envisaged at a World Cup final. Except for Infantino.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal's adorable three-year-old brother steals the show again as he shares heartfelt moment with World Cup winner on the pitch
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lamine Yamal isn't the only member of his family captivating audiences around the world.

The 19-year-old Spanish forward's three-year-old half-brother Keyne has been a breakout star of the World Cup and went viral again on Sunday with his post-game celebration following the 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final.

Dressed in a replica Spain jersey with his brother's No. 19 and his own first name emblazoned on the back, Keyne darted onto the pitch at MetLife Stadium, where he then ran straight into his older brother's arms.

Yamal was all too happy to accept a hug from Keyne and quickly lifted his younger brother into the air before gently placing him back down on the field and putting a red 'Lamine' baseball hat on the toddler's head.

And that wasn't the only hat Keyne tried on while roaming around the MetLife pitch on Sunday. A New Jersey State Trooper couldn't help but remove his cap to briefly share with Keyne, who tried it on before politely returning it to the officer.

For Keyne, it was one of the final moments of a memorable World Cup run that included several appearances on stadium scoreboards, not to mention dozens of wire photos that were picked up by news outlets around the world. Keyne even managed to score a goal on his brother's teammate, Nico Williams, during some pre-game warmups.

Lamine Yamal celebrates with his brother Keyne after winning the 2026 World Cup

Keyne was all smiles when he finally caught up to his big brother, Yamal, after Sunday's win

Keyne, 3, gestures on the field at MetLife Stadium after seeing his brother win Sunday's final

Lamine Yamal puts the World Cup trophy into his younger brother Keyne's arms on Sunday

Keyne is seen dancing near a giant replica of the World Cup trophy on Sunday

Yamal and his brother Keyne bump fists alongside the World Cup trophy on Sunday

'This time around, the biggest sensation of the competition isn't an athlete, the goals, or even the trophy itself,' was how Hola! – Spain's version of Hello! magazine – put it earlier this month. 'It's Keyne, Lamine Yamal's three-year-old brother, who's taking the tournament by storm with his hilarious moments.'

Standing just a few feet tall, Keyne has rapidly become an internet sensation. The toddler has melted hearts throughout Spain's run, endearing himself to supporters across the world.

Elsewhere in the media, he has been dubbed 'the star of the 2026 World Cup,' 'Spain's superstar in the stands' and 'the most beloved personality of the tournament'.

Keyne's popularity reached fever pitch after Spain's quarter-final victory over Belgium, when television cameras cut to the three-year-old waving and smiling at his brother from the stands.

Lamine Yamal and his mother Sheila Ebana attempt to hand the trophy to young Keyne

At just 3, Keyne appears to already have one World Cup victory under his belt

Keyne was given a piece of the goal's net, which he used to entertain a state trooper

A New Jersey state trooper couldn't help but share his hat with Keyne, who tried it on

Keyne was a man of many hats on Sunday, including this offering from a state trooper

Yamal dropped a new baseball hat on his brother's head after Sunday's victory

Down on the pitch, Yamal burst into laughter after spotting Keyne sticking out his tongue on the stadium's giant screens. Images of the youngster's antics were soon circulating across social media.

Speaking to journalists after the match, Yamal revealed his brother had warned him about his plans the day before, making the moment even funnier.

'I was at physio and he called me, using my mum's phone, and told me that he was going to stick his tongue out tomorrow,' the right-winger explained. 'So that's why when I saw him on the screen, it really made me laugh.'

Born in September 2022, Keyne is the son of Yamal's mother, Sheila Ebana. Although the pair do not share the same father, the Barcelona star spoke glowingly about their bond after being named player of the match in Spain's round-of-32 victory last Thursday.

'I'm moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of,' he said.

'My little brother means everything to me. I am in love with him; it feels like he is my son.'

Keyne wasn't happy to just watch Sunday's World Cup final, and instead got some practice in

Keyne impresses onlookers at MetLife Stadium with some fancy footwork

For those who have followed Yamal's rise closely, Keyne's presence is nothing new. The footballer regularly shares videos of them doing TikTok dances together, while clips of the pair playing with a football on the pitch during Barcelona's La Liga title celebrations last season also went viral.

There is footage of Keyne singing the Barcelona anthem at home and cheering his brother's name. He has been filmed joking around with Barca's giant mascot, Cat, and spending time with Yamal's close friend and Spain team-mate Nico Williams after a La Liga match between Barcelona and Athletic Club. Yamal also recently shared a video of him and his mum walking down the street together, behind Keyne driving a Mercedes electric kids car.

When Yamal gave a tour of his former Barcelona flat at the end of last year, he proudly showed viewers a small statuette depicting him squatting and said it was Keyne's 'favourite thing in my house'. The figure references the traditional Catalan caganer – typically hidden within Nativity scenes and portrayed relieving itself outside the stable – and Keyne appears especially delighted that his older brother has his own version.

Keyne took a quick breather during Sunday's festivities before getting his second wind

Keyne is joined by another Spanish supporter on Sunday in East Rutherford, New jersey

Yamal, who brought Keyne with him to the Ballon d'Or ceremony, has previously spoken about wanting to give his younger brother the childhood he never had. The winger has made his famous '304' celebration – a reference to the postcode of Rocafonda, one of Catalonia's most deprived neighborhoods where he grew up – a symbol of his identity and a nod to his roots.

'My mom had me when she was 16 – now that's real pressure,' he told Spanish broadcaster Cadena SER. 'Then my dad had to go out and make a living, scavenging on the streets to bring food home. That's pressure. All I have to do is play and keep the Spanish fans happy.'

'I came from an apartment where the kitchen and bedroom were in the same place,' he said on a podcast last year. 'So I see my mother happy, I see that my brother can have the kind of childhood I would have wanted, and that's what makes me happiest.'

Keyne is also a familiar face on his mother's Instagram profile, appearing in sponsored posts, including a recent promotion for a sushi restaurant in Premià de Mar, a coastal town near Barcelona.

'Sunday, sushi and good company,' she wrote on Instagram.

Keyne and Yamal are pictured with their mother Sheila Ebana after Spain's Euros win in 2024

This photo taken in 2007 shows a 20-year-old Lionel Messi helping to bathe Lamine Yamal, who was merely six months old at the time. Yamal's mother Sheila Ebana is also pictured

Ebana's eldest son also has some memorable photos from his youth, including one famously taken alongside then-Barcelona star Lionel Messi in 2007.

Yamal's parents, including his Morocco-born father Mounir Nasraoui, entered a raffle run by Catalan newspaper Sport with winners getting photos taken of their baby with a Barcelona player.

Yamal's family famously won and was paired with Messi.

In the shoot, Messi bathed the five-month-old Yamal and then held him, wrapped in a towel.

That picture, it was crazy,' Messi said Friday. 'Him as a baby, and now we are facing each other. What a crazy picture.'

Who knows, if the 39-year-old Messi can hang on a bit longer, perhaps he can face off with the family's other viral star, Keyne, someday.

Sports.title: Donald Trump ignores FIFA president's call to leave the stage as he joins Spain's World Cup final trophy lift in awkward moment
Sports.content:
Donald Trump took center stage at MetLife Stadium on Sunday as he awkwardly invaded Spain's iconic trophy lift at the end of the FIFA World Cup final.

The European champions clinched their second World Cup title after beating Lionel Messi's Argentina 1-0 in extra time, following a late strike from forward Ferran Torres.

Shortly after the full-time whistle, the President made his way down to the field, where he was loudly booed by the crowd before making his way onto the stage alongside FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

Donald Trump took center stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

The President, along with FIFA chief Gianni Infantino, presented the trophy to Spain's Rodri

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away - but the President remained where he was

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained where he was.

He stood to the side of the team as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5 to 1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage once again.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the pair undoubtedly clear.

Prior to the official trophy lift, Trump also handed out silver medals to Argentina's players - including Messi - after their heartbreaking defeat in New Jersey.

Fans noted that one Argentina star - Tottenham defender Cristian Romero - completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from Infantino before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, the President also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball - which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

Trump and Infantino stood on stage as golden confetti rained down around them in New Jersey

The US President welcomed Spain's stars onto the stage before presenting the prestigious title

The President also handed out silver medals to Lionel Messi and Argentina after their loss

Trump pictured presenting Lamine Yamal with his medal after the 1-0 win at MetLife Stadium

Argentina defender Cristian Romero appeared to ignore Trump as he walked on stage

There was a degree of irony in regards to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite - alongside FIFA President Infantino, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump also shook hands with Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the president. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, reportedly watched the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump cozied up to FIFA President Gianni Infantino in the private suite on Sunday afternoon in New Jersey

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the president's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania joined the massive crowd at MetLife Stadium for the 2026 World Cup final

Trump also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the President's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

Ahead of the match, Trump told Fox News' Jenny Taft on the FIFA Red Carpet that 'it's hard to bet against Messi,' speaking of Argentina's 39-year-old star.

However, in the end, it wasn't to be for the veteran soccer star after he and Argentina came up short in their battle against European outfit Spain in East Rutherford.

The match was decided by a ferocious, close-range strike from Spanish star Torres in the 106th minute, after a 0-0 stalemate at the end of regulation time.

However, there were ugly scenes once the full-time whistle blew - with a number of frustrated Argentina stars taking out their anger on Spain's players after their loss.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Lionel Messi's bid for back-to-back World Cup titles ended in failure after their loss to Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win over Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those only came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they committed 24 fouls - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Elsewhere on the day, World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Madonna's performance during the World Cup half-time show divided fans

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed her hit Dai Dai with Burna Boy

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with only a guitar to sing a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Sports.title: Distraught Lionel Messi bursts into tears as his World Cup career ends in heartbreak after brutal loss to Spain
Sports.content:
A heartbroken Lionel Messi burst into tears on the pitch after collecting his runners-up medal in what will almost certainly be his final ever World Cup appearance.

The Argentina captain - who spent most of his career playing in Barcelona - was ineffectual against Spain in the New Jersey showdown as his team failed to find the net in 120 minutes.

The tournament in America was almost certainly Messi's final international bow, and his emotional full-time reaction went some way to confirming that.

When the final whistle blew, he dropped to the ground and held his hands to his face, inconsolable by his teammates and opponents alike.

After gathering himself to collect his runners-up medal from Donald Trump, the emotions of the moment became too much for the sport's greatest-of-all-time as he burst into tears just before Spain lifted the trophy.

Messi's career will continue with Inter Miami but he is unlikely to play at the highest level again for his country, given he will be 43 when the next World Cup takes place.

Lionel Messi let the tears flow just moments after collecting his World Cup runners-up medal

At the end of what was likely his last World Cup game, Messi appeared inconsolable

In a heartbreaking scene, he sat alone on the turf at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium

Messi was appearing in his third World Cup final, four years after he lifted the trophy for his country in Qatar.

His first time in the biggest game of them all came in 2014 in Brazil, when he and his countrymen were beaten in extra-time by Germany.

It was the same result for the heartbroken Messi on Sunday, as Spain's Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game deep into the additional 30-minute period.

In the game itself, Messi struggled to make an impact against the country he knows so well, barely getting a kick against the likes of Lamine Yamal and Co.

As an estimated 1.7 billion people watched on from around the world, waiting for Messi to produce the magic we so often see from him, he struggled to find the pace of the game and could not help his team to victory.

Messi sits on the grass at MetLife and watches Spain's players celebrate their triumph

It is unlikely football fans will ever see the great man grace the World Cup stage ever again

Eric Garcia hugs Messi on the pitch at the end of a hard-fought 1-0 Spain win in New Jersey

Join the discussion How should Messi's World Cup legacy be remembered after this emotional farewell?

After collecting his losers' medal from Trump, he stood in front of the Argentina fans inside the stadium, letting the emotion pour out of him.

On X, one fan wrote of the moment: 'You aren't a football fan if you don't feel sad for Messi.'

A second added: 'Thanks for everything you put into this game. You'll always be the best.'

A third, meanwhile, said: 'Damn, the greatest of all time. The best to ever do it.'

Sports.title: Spain 1-0 Argentina: Ferran Torres' extra time winner secures World Cup trophy for Luis de la Fuente's side - as Lionel Messi suffers tournament heartbreak
Sports.content:
Spain 1-0 Argentina: Ferran Torres' extra time winner secures World Cup trophy for Luis de la Fuente's side - as Lionel Messi suffers tournament heartbreak

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The voice of Frank Sinatra rang around the MetLife Stadium before the World Cup final. As he sang about facing the ‘final curtain’, the big screen showed footage of Lionel Messi holding aloft the World Cup in Qatar four years ago and being borne shoulder-high by his teammates in triumph. ‘I did it my way,’ Sinatra sang, as the Manhattan skyscrapers shimmered in the distance.

In times when football has lost itself, when it has moved away from those who love it, when it has become enslaved to money and ruled by high ticket prices, when it is led by sycophants and grifters, when it has been assailed by doubts about its integrity and its direction, Messi has always been there to redeem it, doing it his way.

This time, in the midst of this drab, angry, bitter, attritional final, doing it his way was not enough. This time, he could not redeem even his own team, who behaved with a despicable lack of grace and barely contained thuggery after the final whistle and who were utterly outclassed by Spain. Spain only won 1-0. It should have been many more.

At a World Cup afflicted by a myriad of controversies, a World Cup with a final saddled with a dirge of a half-time show and hydration breaks that are advertising breaks and President Trump calling Gianni Infantino to lobby, successfully, for Folarin Balogun’s suspension to be lifted, and $1m pitchside seats, seeing Messi play was always enough to make the heart sing.

Even at 39, the greatest player the world has ever seen, has still been the sport’s human shield. Even as Trump and Infantino have danced around the tournament like puppeteers, Messi has worked his magic, scored more goals than anyone apart from Kylian Mbappe and floated above the storms.

Spain have won the World Cup after Ferran Torres' extra time winner against Argentina

Torres smashed in the winner with his left foot after Nico Williams headed the ball back across goal

It was elation for the Spanish players as they celebrated wildly in the corner of the stadium

But it was devastation for Argentina's crestfallen stars, who had fought for their lives

Messi has graced his sport for more than 20 years and Argentina’s obstinate, defiant, sometimes desperate run to this World Cup final against Spain was predicated around this being ‘Leo’s last one’. They wanted to do it for him. They wanted to give him the send-off he deserved before he retreated to what remains of his club career with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.

And so Messi went to the well one last time in the blazing sunshine in New Jersey. Fifteen of his 21 tournament goals have come since his 35th birthday and even though Mbappe had moved ahead of him in the race for the Golden Boot on Saturday evening and ahead of him in the all-time World Cup list, many hoped Messi would put that right on Sunday, too.

The truth is that when Messi went to the well this time, the well was empty. This was a game too far, even for him. Tom Cruise had given a speech on the pitch before kick-off and this match turned into Messi’s mission impossible.

He was swallowed up in the mediocrity of a final that was at odds with so much of the drama that this World Cup has provided. It was dull and attritional. It was dominated by Spain, who finally turned their advantage into a winning goal in the second period of extra time.

And if many wanted Messi to win, by then not many wanted Argentina to win. They played with a mixture of unabashed thuggery and a desperate lack of ambition. They did not have a single shot in normal time, let alone a shot on target. If there was a shred of satisfaction about their defrocking, it was that it came with an overdue red card for Enzo Fernandez, their self-styled enforcer, at the end of normal time.

So Messi’s final fling fell flat. He did not end the competition with the Golden Boot, he did not win the second World Cup he craved, and he left the international stage after being able to exert precious little influence on his final match. Sport is no respecter of reputation.

Torres' goal sparked jubilation for the thousands of Spanish fans inside the stadium

Argentina keeper Emiliano Martinez had been in inspired form before that to keep Spain at bay

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

Enzo Fernandez was sent off at the end of normal time for a reckless second bookable offence

A melee ensued and Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth

Much of the talk before the game had been about a passing of the torch from Messi to Spain’s superstar teenager Lamine Yamal but even if Yamal had more influence than Messi, he has been struggling with the after-effects of a hamstring injury and could not stamp his brilliance on the game.

It was Ferran Torres who made the difference when he came on, Ferran Torres who scored the winner and Ferran Torres who thought he had scored a second before it was ruled out for offside. This was Spain’s second World Cup triumph after 2010. They only conceded one goal in the entire competition. They were the better team by a large margin here.

Yamal had the first chance of the game within the opening five minutes. A neat touch from Dani Olmo played Yamal in behind the Argentina defence but he did not hit his shot with enough power or accuracy to beat Emiliano Martinez.

Argentina had not started the game with the same furious intent they showed against England in the semi-final. Not driven by the same visceral resentment, they showed Spain far more respect and allowed them to dictate the tempo of the game.

Spain had only conceded one goal in the tournament before this game but they had a scare early on when Messi raced on to a through ball. He was clean through but Unai Simon sprinted 35 yards out of his goal to clear it and got there just ahead of Argentina’s skipper. Some felt Messi had missed an opportunity. ‘He had to put his body in and he didn't,' Wayne Rooney said.

Alexis Mac Allister scythed down Olmo after 15 minutes but, inexplicably, referee Slavko Vincic, chose not to show him even a yellow card. The Spain fans were infuriated. They are keenly aware of the lenient treatment Argentina have benefited from in this World Cup. ‘Infantino, Infantino,’ they jeered.

Argentina did their best to rile up Spain and there were several flashpoints between the players

Things escalated at full-time when Leandro Paredes clashed with several Spain players

The stands were filled with celebrities, including David Beckham and Tom Cruise (centre)

President Donald Trump also watched on alongside FIFA President Gianni Infantino

The pair later presented the players with their medals and handed over the trophy to Spain

Justin Bieber headlined the strange half-time show, which lasted for almost half an hour

The game settled into a kind of stalemate, the antithesis of the Soccer Aid vibe that permeated England’s third-place play-off game with France the previous day. There was, at least, a ripple of surprise when the referee booked Lisandro Martinez. It was just about the only decision that had gone Spain’s way all afternoon.

The half-time show came and went in a splurge of underwhelming banality. It was much like the opening 45 minutes, in which Argentina had not managed a single shot on target. Leandro Paredes came on at the interval and was booked within a few minutes for a shove in the back of Max Baena.

Yamal made one burst to the byline midway through the second half and cut the ball back for substitute Ferran Torres. Torres leapt well on the edge of the six-yard box but could only direct his header straight at a grateful Emiliano Martinez.

As the game approached extra time, Argentina imploded. More particularly, Enzo Fernandez imploded. Already on a yellow card, he launched himself into a tackle on Pau Cubarsi and caught the defender’s trailing foot. Cubarsi cart-wheeled into the air and Fernandez was shown a second yellow. It felt like a little karma for the rough-house tactics he had inflicted on England in Atlanta and for which he had escaped without punishment.

Increasingly, only Emiliano Martinez kept Argentina in the game. He saved well from a Yamal free kick and then, early in extra time, from a glancing header by Nico Williams. Spain thought they had scored when Martinez spilled the ball under a challenge but VAR ruled that he had been fouled. It felt like another generous decision towards Argentina.

Spain missed the best chance of the match when Arsenal’s Mikel Merino glanced a header wide from close range near the end of the first half of extra time but they finally broke the deadlock after 106 minutes when Williams nodded the ball back to Torres and Torres smashed the ball past Emiliano Martinez.

Their victory was to be celebrated. Messi’s retreat into the twilight was much to be mourned.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has new motive for 64-team World Cup as truth laid bare
Sports.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has new motive for 64-team World Cup as truth laid bare

Like or not, the newly-expanded 48-team World Cup was a bit hit in the United States, Canada and Mexico over the course of the past five weeks

View 3 Images Ferran Torres struck the winner for Spain in the World Cup final

Only in a World Cup that left you wanting more could Argentina decide that we've all seen enough.

‌



That's what transpired as Lionel Scaloni's anti-football left a stain on an otherwise forgettable final that belonged to Spain.

‌



That game aside, it's no wonder FIFA fancy more. It's little wonder Gianni Infantino has already loosely floated expanding the World Cup to an astonishing 64-team tournament by 2030.

‌



Optically, it's a painful and greedy pitch. Naturally, you're sceptical and fearful. When does even more football actually become too much football? But dissect it.

Remove the geopolitics, ignore that FIFA are merely relishing the chance to line their pockets, and brush over the repercussions of increased player workload amid an already jam-packed schedule; beneath all those variables lies the answer.

OPINION FIFA must punish Argentina over three disgraceful World Cup final incidents by Ryan Taylor

‌



What Argentina star said to Rodri in furious on-pitch exchange after World Cup final whistle READ MORE :

Truthfully, no World Cup is ever enough because it always leaves you wanting more. Even when all is said and done, you're still left with unanswered questions as you decompress.

You're left wondering what might have been, you're left wishing the next four years would already pass.

For the record, in these tough scorching mid-summer conditions, on the back of that exhausting yet historic night in Mexico City, the simmering humidity in Miami and that emotional barnburner with Argentina, it's hard to escape the feeling that England may have struggled to turn the dial chasing shadows against obsessive control freaks Spain.

‌



That is of course, besides the point because had the cautious and now heavily-scrutinised Thomas Tuchel not led England into a depressing state of surrender, they would have at least boasted a puncher's chance in a one-off, box-office final.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is open to expanding the World Cup again to 64 in 2030 (Image: MANDEL NGAN, AFP via Getty Images)

It's hard but cast aside the frustrations of those soul-destroying final minutes in Atlanta and on the face of it, you have to say the inflated tournament has worked even if this was international football as we've never seen it before.

‌



It was proof that even when there is political interference, even when dubious red card bans are surprisingly - or unsurprisingly - upheld and concerns regarding the integrity of the competition are raised, the on-pitch action always trumps all.

It will always blitz the half-time showbiz and definitely outshine the razzmatazz of flying nervous La Roja boss Luis de la Fuente to his pre-match press conference via helicopter.

Take the smallest-populated nation at the World Cup, Caribbean Island Curacao (156,000 residents), equalising against heavily-fancied Germany, African minnows Cape Verde pushing the holders Argentina to the wire and their physical limit.

‌



Take DR Congo, who only snuck qualification via the inter-continental play-offs, being just 15 minutes away from eliminating England in their first finals appearance since 1974 when they were thrashed 9-0 by Yugoslavia as Zaire and you come to realise that the World Cup script is never truly written.

View 3 Images England only just squeezed past DR Congo in the World Cup Round of 32 (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

Even if it slightly underwhelmed, the final - a clash of contrasting styles - typified that more than ever because 1,309 days ago, under the world's largest tensile cable-net roof at Lusail Stadium in Doha, Lionel Messi looked to have signed off in quintessential style after firing La Albiceleste to a prestigious third star.

‌



It was the crowning moment for football's king so for him to even make this tournament in the midst of his 39th birthday, let alone score eight goals and record four assists on a long-winding and intense road to the final, is in many respects, indicative of his legacy.

Messi belongs to the history books, it was a privilege to once again witness his genius first-hand and a further reminder as to why the World Cup will always remain the greatest show on earth.

Infantino insists this tournament was the best of the lot. Even if you do not happen to agree, unfortunately you can make a case for it and for that reason, it was undeniably, despite all the ridiculous side-stories and distractions, it will ultimately go down as a major success.

Sports.title: Gabby Logan warns Micah Richards on BBC's World Cup final coverage after Gary Lineker jibes
Sports.content:
Gabby Logan warns Micah Richards on BBC's World Cup final coverage after Gary Lineker jibes

Micah Richards wasn't frightened to make a dig despite being part of the BBC's World Cup final coverage with Gabby Logan, Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart on Sunday night

View 2 Images Gabby Logan warned Micah Richards (Image: BBC)

BBC presenter Gabby Logan sent a swift warning to Micah Richards as he followed in Gary Lineker's footsteps to make fun of the broadcaster's decision to remain in Salford for most of their World Cup coverage. Logan, along with Richards, Wayne Rooney and Joe Hart were at MetLife Stadium for Spain's clash with Argentina but had been consigned to a studio in the United Kingdom for much of the tournament based in the USA, Mexico and Canada.

‌



The BBC's decision drew some mockery in comparison to ITV's New York studio, and it appears that choice might have even frustrated some of the channel's pundits. The hot topic came to the forefront as the top of World Cup highlights came in conversation.

‌



While Logan highlighted that none of her colleagues had praised the supporters present throughout the tournament, particularly Norway's Viking antics, Richards took an opportunity to make a dig. The former Manchester City star acknowledged that they had not had the opportunity to experience the impact of supporters on the tournament, despite still working for the broadcaster on the night.

‌



"Nobody said fans," Logan said. "I think the fans have been incredible at this tournament. Every single nation, but there were certain countries like Norway. Fans who really lit it up."

Richards quipped: "There are not that many fans in Salford!" Logan returned: "You can't say the S-word again."

“This will be exciting and something very different but still very similar to the podcast.”

Sports.title: FIFA must punish Argentina over three disgraceful World Cup final incidents
Sports.content:
FIFA must punish Argentina over three disgraceful World Cup final incidents

Argentina laid on a clinic in how not to play and how not to behave in their World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was sent off for violent conduct

Should that be the last we ever see of Lionel Messi at a World Cup - it was a sorry way to bow out.

‌



Argentina's tournament ended in disgrace and despite their captain's genius, he could not totally distance himself from what can only be described as a national embarrassment.

‌



After all, it was the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner who tried to engineer Marc Cucurella's dismissal in a sheer act of desperation

‌



The newly-signed Real Madrid left-back admittedly briefly covered his mouth but the 39-year-old veteran and Enzo Fernandez's unsuccessful attempts to snitch on and intimidate Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic were shameful and smacked of desperation.

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final READ MORE :

What Argentina star said to Rodri in furious on-pitch exchange after World Cup final whistle READ MORE :

The great irony was that not only did Fernandez later get sent off following two yellow cards but Nicolas Otamendi also had the audacity to accuse Rodri and Aymeric Laporte of deliberately trying to influence the officials.

The worst - Leandro Paredes' full-time thuggery - was yet to come - however. Losing your cool is one thing but Paredes lost all sense of self-respect as he jostled, wrestled and attacked Eric Garcia and Gavi.

‌



Special mention to right-back Nahuel Molina for not only playing a key part in Ferran Torres' winner but also punching Rodri.

FIFA are yet to punish Argentina's controversial and offensive 'Islas Malvinas' banner post-England but it's about time they threw the book at Lionel Scaloni's side, who also lost huge respect on the day they vacated their World Cup crown.

Paredes and Molina's behaviour in particular was unsavoury, shocking and utterly unsurprising if you watched him in action against England in Atalanta.

‌



His sole primary purpose on the pitch is to startle the opposition and get under their skin. Little wonder he's earned 84 caps.

View 3 Images EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JULY 19: Leandro Paredes of Argentina (5) gets violent against Gavi of Spain (9) after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Even Scaloni's assistant coach Raton Ayala thought it was acceptable to put his fist into the face of Spain's Dani Olmo, this is another separate incident that requires policing.

‌



Rather mysteriously, Valentin Barco was nowhere to be seen. He was happy to shout and celebrate wildly - invading the field from the bench - in the face of Jude Bellingham but when Spain were crowned champions, he was nowhere to be seen.

Fernandez's midweek 'Wonderwall' Instagram post mocking England also backfired spectacularly and blew up in his face.

Argentina then took it upon themselves to turn their backs to Spain as La Roja made their way onto the podium to lift the iconic gold trophy - it was a staggering lack of basic respect.

‌



This is all without considering how badly Argentina actually played. They did not have a single shot until the 116th minute.

View 3 Images Lionel Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Spain centre-back Laporte actually referenced that both he and his teammates felt Argentina went overboard in midweek.

‌



The newly-crowned world champions do not do things in half measures and therefore, saw no reason to revel in the glory of Tuesday's semi-final triumph over France.

Scaloni claimed his players were a "great example for our people and country," and ultimately, if they are honestly a true reflection of the nation's population, it's hard to see Argentina ever being universally popular.

It's a miracle the final was so one-sided when you consider the South Americans were also the only team not to have a single VAR intervention against them, they received the most penalties, had the most opposition goals chalked off, the most opposition yellow cards awarded and they also travelled the least out of all the 48 competing nations.

Article continues below

Equally, it would have been the biggest injustice since Folarin Balogun's red card was overturned had Argentina won.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Deal agreed for third summer signing as PSG star set to leave
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Deal agreed for third summer signing as PSG star set to leave

Liverpool round-up as one of the Europe's most exciting young players becomes available

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola has had some good news in the transfer market (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

A crucial pre-season is underway at Liverpool as Andoni Iraola attempts to revive the club's fortunes following a torrid title defence. Preparations will move up a notch next weekend when the Reds face Sunderland in Nashville.

‌



Further friendlies in the US, against Wrexham and Leeds United, will follow before home games against Monaco and Como ahead of the Premier League opener at Newcastle on August 23.

‌



Two new players have joined the club so far this summer, with Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz arriving from Rennes and Osasuna, respectively. However, much more remedial work is needed if Liverpool are to launch a title challenge this season.

‌



World Cup stars Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola are among a host of players to be linked with a move to Anfield. As new campaign edges closer, here's a round-up of some of the latest Reds news…

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Reds beat Bayern

Liverpool have beaten Bayern Munich to the signing of Samuel Martinez. As reported by the Liverpool Echo, the Reds have agreed a fee of around £740,000 with Atletico Nacional for the attacking midfielder.

‌



As part of the deal, he will remain at the Colombian side for a further 12 months and will arrive during next summer's transfer window after turning 18 in April. The 17-year-old was wanted by a host of European giants, including Barcelona and Borussia Dortmund.

It has also emerged that Bayern were strong contenders for Martinez's signature. The youngster had been on the radar of the German champions for months and was on their summer target list, reports TZ . Bayern scouts are said to have likened Martinez's style of play to that of Brazilian legend Kaka.

They also had a trump card in the shape of the player's agent, Daniel Neumuller, who is from Bavaria. However, it is Liverpool who appear to have won the race to sign him, even if fans will have to wait a year to see him in the flesh.

‌



Mbaye on the move

The Reds have been put on alert after Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris Saint-Germain was made available for transfer. It's no secret that the Reds are in the market for a wide man or two.

View 2 Images Ibrahim Mbaye looks set to leave PSG (Image: Getty Images)

Hopes of signing Diomande appear to have faded, with the Ivorian reportedly holding out for a move to PSG and prepared to spend another season at RB Leipzig. Therefore, Liverpool may turn to 18-year-old Mbaye, one of the most exciting young talents in Europe.

‌



According to Fabrizio Romano, the Senegal star will leave PSG this summer, with super agent Jorge Mendes said to be "in control of his future." The report adds that Premier League and Bundesliga clubs are on standby to take advantage of the situation.

While competition will be intense, the Reds would be an attractive proposition given the obvious vacancy on the right flank following Mohamed Salah's departure .

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
